memory_candidates.content: Cross-script content-hashing contracts have a silent staleness failure mode: when script A computes a digest over content script B generates, and A strips a known-varying line set before hashing, any later addition of per-invocation-varying content to B's template silently invalidates A's normalization -- and neither script's own tests catch it, because B's tests only check B's output and A's tests use hand-written fixtures frozen at A's authoring time. The symptom is a guard that goes inert rather than failing loudly: every downstream back-out step of the guard appears broken at once, which looks like many bugs but is one upstream predicate never satisfied. Two structural fixes together, not either alone: (1) a forward-pointer comment in the GENERATING script at each varying interpolation site, pointing at the normalizer's strip pattern; (2) an isolated unit-level fixture over the normalizer enumerating ALL known varying locations, so a new one fails a cheap test rather than silently degrading an expensive live-pipeline guard.

verify-deploy.sh's gate 13 (whole-tree orphan detection) can legitimately fail for reasons entirely unrelated to the task at hand: the deploy copy engine is additive-only by design (context/patterns/deploy-orphan-detection.md), so a file quarantined/deleted from the source store in an EARLIER, unrelated commit stays stranded in the deployed .claude/ tree forever until a human or explicitly-scoped task deletes it. Before treating a gate-13 or run-all.sh --fail-on-new failure as caused by your own edits, diff your own edited source files against their deployed counterparts (should be byte-identical) and check git log/blame on the failing suite/file to confirm it predates your changes -- this cheaply separates 'my fix is incomplete' from 'pre-existing unrelated drift, record as a reasoned exclusion and move on'.
